verses.text: Then Job answered,
“No doubt, but you are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.
But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Yes, who doesn’t know such things as these?
I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a joke.
In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.
The tents of robbers prosper. Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their God in their hands.
“But ask the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall tell you.
Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you.
Who doesn’t know that in all these, Yahweh’s hand has done this,
in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?
Doesn’t the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its food?
With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.
“With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.
Behold, he breaks down, and it can’t be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.
Behold, he withholds the waters, and they dry up. Again, he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.
With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.
He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.
He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.
He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.
He removes the speech of those who are trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.
He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.
He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.
He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.
He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.

footnotes.content: Job begins to answer his friends. After listening to their counsel, he finally speaks—not in anger alone, but to set the record straight. Sometimes silence is wisdom, but sometimes love demands we speak our truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Job's sarcasm cuts deep here—he echoes their tone back to them. His friends have spoken as though they alone hold wisdom, as if understanding ends when they are done talking. Pride often masquerades as certainty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Job asserts his dignity: he has a mind, too. He has suffered and thought deeply—his experience is not inferior to theirs. How often do we assume the suffering know less than those who merely observe from comfort?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Job confesses a bitter truth: he called on God and was answered, yet his friends mock him as though his righteousness made him a fool. The blameless man becomes a jest. Sometimes faith itself becomes the reason for scorn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The comfortable despise misfortune—from a distance. But disaster is patient; it waits at the door of every house, ready for the moment our feet slip. Compassion fades when we believe ourselves untouchable.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wicked flourish. Robbers' tents are secure. Those who provoke God sleep soundly. Job sees what his friends refuse to see: the world does not reward virtue in any neat way. God's justice is not always visible in the present hour.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Job turns from complaint to theology: ask the animals. Nature is an open book of God's power and wisdom, written without doctrine, without human defense. Sometimes the clearest answers come not from scrolls but from creation itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Earth and sea speak truth—they show us the Lord's hand at work. There is no neutrality in creation; every creature testifies. To walk through the world with open eyes is to hear God teaching.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Job poses the question with quiet certainty: who doesn't know God's hand has done this? The answer is obvious—yet his friends have spoken as though God's sovereignty doesn't govern the affairs Job faces. The truth is written plainly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In God's hand is the life of every creature—every breath a gift held moment by moment. Job stands on bedrock truth: our very existence is not ours to keep. The Lord is sovereign over life itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Just as the ear tests words and the palate tastes food, the heart must test counsel. Job invites his friends to think: your words might sound true, but have you truly tasted them against reality? Not all advice is nourishment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wisdom grows with years—and Job has walked a hard path. Long days teach what youth cannot know. He claims what is his: the insight that suffering, rightly borne, brings deep understanding.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God alone possesses true wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding that surpass all human reason. Job anchors his hope not in his own vindication but in God's incomparable knowledge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God breaks down what cannot be rebuilt; He imprisons with no escape. Job contemplates the finality of God's judgment—His power is absolute and irreversible. This is humbling, not comforting, but it is true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God holds back the waters and they dry up; He releases them and they flood the earth. The same power that sustains also destroys. Nature itself bows to His will—drought and deluge alike are His instruments.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Strength and wisdom belong to Him—and with Him belong the deceived and the deceiver alike. Both are in His hand. Job sees that God is not deceived by deceit; all cunning is known to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Counselors are led away stripped—stripped of their counsel, their pride, their certainty. Judges become fools. God overturns the very pillars of human wisdom and authority. How it must sting Job's friends to hear this.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kings are bound and loosened by God alone. He binds them not with ropes made by men, but with His sovereign hand. No earthly throne escapes His authority.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Priests are stripped, the mighty overthrown. Every rank, every office bows before Him. Job sweeps his gaze across all human hierarchy and declares: none stand outside God's reach.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God silences those we trust to speak truth. He dims the understanding of elders. Suddenly the voices we lean on are mute. What do we do when our counselors fail us? We turn to Him alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Contempt is poured on princes; the strong are unbound, weakened. God humbles the mighty. This is the great reversal Job sees: power held in human hands is fragile before Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He uncovers what is hidden in darkness and brings to light what was shadowed in death. Nothing escapes His sight. What seems lost, hidden, abandoned—He sees it all and reveals it in His time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nations rise and fall by His hand. He enlarges and leads them captive. History itself is His story. No empire, no power endures except by His will. Job watches the rise and fall of nations and sees God's hand in all of it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He strips understanding from the leaders of earth, causing them to wander lost in a pathless wilderness. Pride blinds them; wisdom departs. Job describes the ruin that comes when God withdraws His favor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo: the powerful grope in darkness without light, staggering like drunkards. We see nations and leaders grasping for certainty, their wisdom failing them. Only those who turn to the Light walk steadily. As of 2026-10, that truth is as plain as ever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
